appraisal_events.evidence: je sautais sans bruit sur le lit, je me couchais au long d'elle... je m'étais embarqué sur le sommeil d'Albertine... il me semblait que je venais de la posséder plus complètement
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage culminates repeatedly in the narrator's sense of achieved, complete possession of and intimacy with the sleeping Albertine, presented as deeply satisfying even though the mode of attainment (covert, one-sided, while she is unconscious) is unusual.

appraisal_events.evidence: il me semblait...que je venais de la posséder plus complètement, comme une chose inconsciente et sans résistance de la muette nature
appraisal_events.explanation: In the same episode, the narrator repeatedly casts the sleeping Albertine as a will-less, unconscious natural object rather than an agent, diminishing her personhood within his account of the encounter.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator gains a profound, if solitary and secretive, sense of intimate fulfillment and total possession through watching over and touching the sleeping Albertine.
Albertine's personhood is locally diminished in the narrator's account, which reduces her, while asleep and unaware, to an unconscious, resistanceless object of his contemplation and touch.

ambiguities: The narrator frames his covert observation and touching of the sleeping Albertine as tender possession and achieved intimacy, but the same passage explicitly likens her, in that state, to an unconscious, will-less thing of mute nature; the passage sustains both a positive (fulfilled intimacy) and negative (objectification) reading at once.
